Links: [{"title":"nextjs16 proxy middleware","url":"https://smithery.ai/skills/jordinodejs/nextjs16-proxy-middleware"},{"title":"Smithery Logo","url":"https://smithery.ai/skills/MUmerRazzaq/better-auth"},{"title":"better-auth.com","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/1.6/integrations/next.md"},{"title":"# Next.js integration (/docs/integrations/next)","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/integrations/next.md"},{"title":"NextJS 16 Proxy issues","url":"https://community.vercel.com/t/nextjs-16-proxy-issues/27780"},{"title":"You are currently viewing documentation for v1.8 (Beta)","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/beta/integrations/next"},{"title":"You are currently viewing documentation for v1.6","url":"https://better-auth.com/docs/1.6/integrations/next"},{"title":"proxy and protected routes","url":"https://blog.vercel.com/academy/subscription-store/proxy-and-protected-routes.md"},{"title":"# Session Handling","url":"https://makerkit.dev/docs/md/nextjs-prisma/authentication/session-handling"}]

The search returned Better Auth documentation on Next.js 16 proxy session protection, but nothing on Auth.js maintenance status, so that half of your query is unanswered.

**Better Auth with Next.js 16 proxy:**
- The Better Auth docs say Next.js 16 renamed middleware to proxy, and they recommend a lightweight cookie-only check in the proxy for redirects, so the proxy doesn't make API or database calls. In Next.js proxy/middleware, it's recommended to only check for the existence of a session cookie to handle redirection to avoid blocking requests by making API or database calls.
- For full validation, the docs show a `proxy.ts` that calls `auth.api.getSession` with the request headers and redirects to sign-in if no session exists. You can use the Node.js runtime for full session validation with database checks, per the docs.
- A community Vercel thread reports a session check breaking after a move to the Node.js proxy approach, though the poster said a later change fixed it. The poster also couldn't explain why the server-side auth worked locally but not on Vercel. My better-auth session check broke. I was using their better-fetch solution and after I noticed it wasn't working properly, I moved to their newer nodejs/proxy middleware solution.
- Makerkit's docs treat the proxy as a first gate only. The proxy is a first gate, not the only gate. Always verify with getSession() in components that handle sensitive data.
- Common pitfalls include headers() Sync Async (await) in Next.js 16 and the fact that Edge runtime in proxy is not supported.

**Auth.js maintenance status:** Not covered by these results. A follow-up search on Auth.js (formerly NextAuth) and its current maintenance status would be needed to answer that part.

Links: [{"title":"better-auth vs NextAuth vs Clerk — Authentication Comparison 2026","url":"https://supastarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-nextauth-vs-clerk"},{"title":"Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth: Which Authentication for Next.js SaaS in 2026","url":"https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk"},{"title":"better auth vs clerk vs nextauth vs auth js 2026 best authentication for next js","url":"https://ldap.kayako.com/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-auth-js-2026-best-authentication-for-next-js.html"},{"title":"better auth vs clerk vs nextauth vs auth js best authentication for next 2026","url":"https://ldap.kayako.com/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-auth-js-best-authentication-for-next-2026.html"},{"title":"Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth (2026)","url":"https://www.turbostarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-supabase-auth"},{"title":"# Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth: Which Authentication for Next.js SaaS in 2026","url":"https://makerkit.dev/blog/md/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk"},{"title":"best auth library nextjs 2026","url":"https://blog.logrocket.com/best-auth-library-nextjs-2026/"},{"title":"better auth vs clerk vs nextauth vs auth js best authentication for next js apps in 2025","url":"https://ldap.kayako.com/better-auth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-auth-js-best-authentication-for-next-js-apps-in-2025.html"},{"title":"ultimate next js auth comparison 2025 betterauth vs clerk vs nextauth vs auth js","url":"https://ldap.kayako.com/ultimate-next-js-auth-comparison-2025-betterauth-vs-clerk-vs-nextauth-vs-auth-js.html"}]

The results lean toward Better Auth or Supabase Auth for new Next.js SaaS projects in 2026, with Clerk and Auth.js as narrower options. Most of the sources are vendor-adjacent blogs, so treat the verdicts as opinion.

- **Better Auth:** One vendor-neutral guide calls it the most complete feature set of the group, with 2FA, passkeys, and RBAC built in, and says it runs in your own infrastructure. It recommends Better Auth for a TypeScript-native library that keeps users in your own Postgres, with first-class multi-tenancy. Its v1 shipped in early 2025, per LogRocket.
- **Auth.js (formerly NextAuth):** Its v5 reached stable in late 2024 as a near-complete rewrite. Reviewers call it mature with a large community, but say it lacks built-in 2FA, passkeys, or RBAC. One guide calls it a legacy choice that teams keep mainly because they already use it.
- **Clerk:** A hosted service with prebuilt UI. One guide notes it gets expensive past 50,000 MAU and locks your user data in a US database. Another lists pricing as a Pro plan at $25/mo plus $0.02 per monthly retained user over 50k.
- **Supabase Auth:** The alternative some guides favor, especially if you already use Supabase and want Row Level Security to handle part of authorization.
- **Security caveat:** LogRocket points to CVE-2025-29927, which showed that middleware-only session checks in Next.js can be bypassed. Verify sessions in the data layer or route handlers, not just in middleware.
- **Source quality:** LogRocket argues that many comparison articles were written for Auth.js v4 and older Clerk pricing, so check dates. Several search results were spam-like keyword pages with no content, and I excluded them. One source claims Auth.js is now under Better Auth Inc., but I found no corroboration, so I'd treat that as unverified.

content.text:
Email/password and Google sign-in are in, and `/dashboard` now redirects signed-out users to `/sign-in`. Google sign-in is untested because it needs real credentials. Everything else works against a throwaway database.

I tested sign-up, `/dashboard` redirecting when signed out (307 to `/sign-in`), and `/dashboard` returning 200 with the new session cookie. Lint is clean. `tsc` reports one error, `LayoutProps` not found in `layout.tsx`, which this change doesn't touch. I didn't render the sign-in or sign-up forms in a browser.

**Choice: Better Auth, with SQLite via `better-sqlite3`.** I compared it with Auth.js, Clerk and Supabase Auth. These are mostly vendor-adjacent blog posts, so treat them as opinion:
- **Better Auth:** it's TypeScript-native, self-hosted, keeps users in your own database, and has first-class Next.js and Google support. It's also the one the comparisons mostly favour for new Next.js projects.
- **Auth.js:** mature, but reviewers describe it as mostly a legacy pick.
- **Clerk:** hosted, with pricing and data lock-in concerns.
- **Supabase Auth:** makes sense mainly if you already use Supabase, which you don't.
- I didn't find anything on Auth.js's current maintenance status, so that part of the comparison is thin.

**What changed:**
- **`src/lib/auth.ts`, `auth-client.ts`, `app/api/auth/[...all]/route.ts`:** server config, client and the auth endpoint.
- **`src/proxy.ts`:** the Next 16 replacement for middleware. It only checks that a session cookie exists, because Next.js middleware-only checks have been bypassed before (CVE-2025-29927).
- **`dashboard/page.tsx`:** checks the session again and redirects if it's invalid, and has a sign-out button.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`:** `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real session, replacing the "first user" TODO. `listUsers()` and `getUser()` now read from the database.
- **Sign-in and sign-up pages:** `/sign-in` and `/sign-up`, with a "Continue with Google" button on both.
- **`.env.example`:** placeholder secret, URL and Google client ID/secret. I added an exception to `.gitignore` so it can be committed, and `*.db` is now ignored.

**Seed users removed:** Ada and Grace are gone from the old in-memory list. The team list on the dashboard now shows whoever has signed up.

**To run it:**
1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env.local` and fill in the values. For Google, the redirect URI is `http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/google`.
2. Run `npm run db:migrate` once to create the tables.
3. Run `npm run dev`.

I left a local `.env.local` with placeholder Google values and a generated secret, plus a freshly migrated `notely.db` (gitignored).

**Left alone:** `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` show as untracked, but I didn't create them, and I haven't committed anything.

Sources:
- [better-auth vs NextAuth vs Clerk — Authentication Comparison 2026](https://supastarter.dev/blog/better-auth-vs-nextauth-vs-clerk)
- [Better Auth vs Clerk vs NextAuth vs Supabase Auth: Which Authentication for Next.js SaaS in 2026](https://makerkit.dev/blog/tutorials/better-auth-vs-clerk)
- [best auth library nextjs 2026 (LogRocket)](https://blog.logrocket.com/best-auth-library-nextjs-2026/)
- [Better Auth: Next.js integration](https://better-auth.com/docs/integrations/next.md)
